text:
vivian: Hey team — FintechX on a Private deployment needs a one‑page checklist they can hand to their network/security team. They want exact outbound rules/hosts/ports to put in their perimeter firewall and proxy. They asked for per-region IPs if possible and whether domain/SNI allowlisting is enough. Any concise guidance we can send?

nate: TL;DR: prefer DNS/SNI allowlist + port 443. If they insist on IPs, we can give two options: customer‑managed NAT (static EIPs they control) or redwood‑managed egress CIDR pools (softly stable, may change with infra updates).

kate: Add security notes: KMS/HSM control-plane calls, audit logging uploads, and webhook callbacks all use TLS on 443. Recommend terminating TLS at the customer perimeter only for inspection — SNI allowlist is acceptable for most customers. Call out that we never send traffic to non‑standard outbound ports.

aj: Are the redwood CIDRs guaranteed for long leases? customer wants them in a config that will be valid for 12 months.

nate: They're NOT guaranteed long‑term unless we provision tenant‑specific EIPs/NATs. Our redwood‑managed pools are relatively stable but can be updated (we publish updates). If they need long leases, we offer a pinned‑egress add‑on for Private/Dedicated that assigns static EIPs per account. I can loop in sales/infra if they want that.

vivian: Can you drop a short checklist and an example test they can run from their network?

nate: Sure — paste below. Keep it short in the email to the customer.

--- begin checklist ---
What to allow (minimal):
- Outbound TLS to these hostnames (SNI/DNS allowlist preferred):
  - control.redwood-inference.com
  - api.models.redwood-inference.com
  - kms.redwood-inference.com  (for Private deployments with KMS integrations)
- Ports: 443 outbound (HTTPS)
- Optional: allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) so hostname checks resolve reliably

Optional IP CIDRs (redwood‑managed egress pools, region examples):
```
34.210.48.0/22  # us-east-1 egress pool
34.211.64.0/19  # us-east fallback pool
52.23.128.0/18  # eu-west-1 sample pool
```
Note: these are illustrative; we publish the canonical list at https://status.redwood-inference.com/egress-cidrs and via the infra subscription webhook.

If you need static IPs for a contract period:
- Ask for "pinned‑egress" (Reserved NAT EIPs) for your Private/Dedicated deployment. We will allocate tenant EIPs and provide those exact addresses to whitelist. This requires additional provisioning lead time (~3–7 business days) and a reserved capacity contract for Dedicated.

Proxy support:
- We support outbound HTTP CONNECT proxies. Example tests:
```
# direct SNI test (no proxy)
curl -v https://control.redwood-inference.com/health -I

# via company proxy (HTTP CONNECT)
curl -x http://proxy.corp.local:8080 -I https://control.redwood-inference.com/health
```
--- end checklist ---

kate: Also mention verification steps for them: run the curl tests from inside their DMZ, and provide TLS fingerprints/SNI hostname to their infra team. If customer uses TLS inspection, we recommend they allow SNI for the hostnames above or provide a dedicated proxy with cert bypass for those hosts.

ops-bot: infra/egress: Published latest egress pool manifest (version 2026-03-10) to /infra/egress/pools and pushed notification to customers/subscriptions.

aj: Great — can you confirm where we host the canonical published list? I need the exact URL for the customer doc.

nate: Use https://status.redwood-inference.com/egress-cidrs (this page includes published manifests, timestamped versions, and the subscription webhook). If they request a signed attest, we can provide a signed manifest on request.

vivian: Perfect. I'll send this checklist to FintechX and offer the pinned‑egress option as next step. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kate: :+1: keep an eye on requests that want port 8443 or non‑standard ports — we currently block those from our control plane.

vivian: noted, closing the loop.
